name: Solicit and level trade bids
summary: A general contractor subcontracts most of a building, so every bid needs firm prices from mechanical, electrical, envelope, steel, drywall and twenty or more other trades. For each trade package an estimator writes a scope sheet, the bid coordinator invites prequalified subcontractors and chases coverage, and on bid day quotes pour in during the last hours with exclusions that must be read, levelled and plugged before the lowest compliant price is carried. On construction management work the preconstruction manager recommends the trade to the owner instead. Missed exclusions and unqualified low bidders are the usual errors, and they surface later as buyout gaps and change orders.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B of annual construction revenue, an Ontario head office and regional offices in Western and Atlantic Canada, bidding public and private institutional, commercial and industrial buildings.
baseline.notes: Invitations by email and online plan rooms; levelling in Excel or estimating software; bid depositories used for some mechanical and electrical packages in Western and Atlantic Canada.

unit_of_work: one trade package on one bid
trigger: Estimating issues the trade package list for a stipulated bid, a CM or design-build proposal, a P3 pursuit or a preconstruction tender call.
end_state: A levelled price is carried in the bid or recommended to the owner, and the trade bid file is passed to buyout or filed after the result.

volume.seasonality: Follows bid volume: peaks February to June with the spring public tender season.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate (25-35 packages per bid); consistent with 25+ packages on a large building in beck-leveling.

surge.cause: spring public tender season before and after the government fiscal year-end

evidence.note: Mirrors the organisation file surge on bd-stipulated-bid, since packages follow bids.

systems.name: Take-off and estimating software with Excel bid sheets
Subcontractor prequalification database (questionnaires, insurance and WSIB certificates)
Public tender and bid portals (MERX, Bids&Tenders, Biddingo, provincial portals)

steps.name: Write the trade package scope
steps.description: The estimator lists the specification sections, drawings and addenda in the package, writes a scope sheet of inclusions, exclusions, alternates and separate prices, and notes interfaces with neighbouring trades so quotes can be compared later.

error.defect_description: An interface item (for example fire stopping or equipment pads) is assigned to no package.

evidence.note: A scope matrix built before bid day; times are estimates.

steps.name: Select bidders from the approved list
steps.description: The bid coordinator filters the subcontractor prequalification database by trade, region and approved contract size, skips firms with expired insurance or workers' compensation clearance, and adds local trades who bid this owner before.

error.defect_description: A firm with an expired certificate or too low a limit is invited.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; the organisation file's prequalification database records insurance and WSIB certificates.

steps.name: Send the invitation to tender
steps.description: The bid coordinator emails each bidder the invitation with the document link, scope sheet, closing date and time for trade prices, and how to submit; trade association plan rooms and online bid platforms carry the same notice.

error.defect_description: Wrong closing time or missing drawing link sent.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; email invitations were the norm in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for trades to confirm they will bid
steps.description: Invited subcontractors and suppliers download the documents and reply whether they intend to bid; many do not reply until chased.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; reply time.

steps.name: Chase bid coverage
steps.description: The bid coordinator phones invitees who have not replied and counts committed bidders for the package. Where fewer than three will bid, she asks the estimator for more names and invites them.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Two or fewer trade bids is treated as thin competition in the source; share is an estimate.

steps.name: Answer trade questions
steps.description: The estimator answers trade questions about scope splits from the scope sheet and forwards questions about the design to the consultant through the general contractor's question list.

error.defect_description: An answer to one bidder is not shared with the others.

evidence.note: Questions go in writing to the owner's single contact and are answered by addendum.

steps.name: Forward addenda to trade bidders
steps.description: When the owner issues an addendum the bid coordinator emails it to every committed bidder for the affected packages and asks them to acknowledge it in their price.

error.defect_description: A bidder does not receive an addendum.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; addenda re-issued to trades.

steps.name: Prepare the levelling sheet
steps.description: Before bid day the estimator sets up the levelling sheet with the scope sheet items down the side and a column per bidder, and enters early quotes from suppliers and trades who price ahead of time.

error.defect_description: A scope item is missing from the sheet.

next.condition: prices come directly to the company
package goes through a bid depository

evidence.note: Scope matrix before bid day; depository share (mostly mechanical and electrical in Western and Atlantic Canada) is an estimate.

steps.name: Collect bids from the bid depository
steps.description: For packages the tender requires to go through the local construction association's bid depository, the bid coordinator collects the sealed trade bids after the depository closes, normally about two working days before the prime closing, and copies them into the levelling sheet.

error.defect_description: A depository bid is mis-copied.

control.basis: Bid depository rules named in the tender: trade bids filed with the depository and used as filed

evidence.note: Trade bids close two working days before prime bids; withdrawals up to six hours before prime closing.

steps.name: Receive trade quotes in the final hours
steps.description: Subcontractors and suppliers send their final quotes by email, fax or phone on closing day, most of them within the last hour or two to protect their price, often with exclusions and qualifications attached.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Bids often arrive in the final hours or minutes before the deadline; wait is the time to bid day.

steps.name: Log quotes as they arrive
steps.description: The bid coordinator logs each quote with time, bidder, amount, addenda acknowledged and attached qualifications, and passes it to the estimator for the package.

error.defect_description: Amount or bidder keyed wrongly in the log.

evidence.note: Logging bidder, amount and submission time.

steps.name: Read exclusions into the levelling sheet
steps.description: The estimator reads each quote in full, marks every scope sheet item as included, excluded or unclear for that bidder, and highlights qualifications such as hoisting, permits, winter work or addenda not acknowledged.

error.defect_description: An exclusion buried in the quote is missed and the gap is found at buyout.

evidence.note: Manual levelling takes 2-4 hours per major scope; ignored qualifications become change orders.

steps.name: Clarify scope with bidders
steps.description: The estimator phones the lowest bidders to confirm unclear items, asks for a revised number where an exclusion can be added back, and notes each answer in the sheet.

error.defect_description: A verbal clarification is not confirmed in writing.

evidence.note: Question lists to bidders and documented conversations.

steps.name: Plug missing scope and adjust
steps.description: The estimator adds an allowance or plug for each item a bidder excluded, using another bidder's price or the company's own unit cost, so that all bids are compared on the same scope.

error.defect_description: Plug too low for the excluded work.

evidence.note: Carry unresolved items conservatively.

steps.name: Check the low bidder's qualification
steps.description: The bid coordinator checks the apparent low bidder in the prequalification database for approved size limit, current insurance and workers' compensation clearance, and whether a subcontract bond will be needed for a package of $250,000 or more.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Company subcontractor prequalification policy; subcontract security for packages of $250,000 or more (Nova Scotia guidelines 4.3)

next.condition: low bidder not on the approved list
low bidder over its limit; next bidder carried

evidence.note: Subcontract security at $250,000; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Prequalify an unlisted bidder quickly
steps.description: The prequalification analyst reviews the unlisted firm's questionnaire, safety statistics, insurance and workers' compensation certificates and recent work, and sets a provisional limit or rejects it, often within hours on bid day.

error.defect_description: Provisional approval given on incomplete documents.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; prequal-analyst is an organisation file role not listed for this process.

steps.name: Select the carried price
steps.description: The estimator picks the lowest compliant levelled price, or the company's own estimate with a plug where coverage failed, and passes the carried number and bidder name to the bid summary.

error.defect_description: Price carried without its plugs.

next.condition: minor package on a stipulated bid

evidence.note: Select on more than price; split by package type is an estimate.

steps.name: Review the major package levelling
steps.description: The chief estimator looks over the levelling sheet for the largest packages, questions plugs and any bid far below the rest, and confirms the carried price before it goes into the final number.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: A bid 15% below all other qualified bidders warrants scrutiny.

steps.name: Name the subcontractor on the bid form
steps.description: For trades the owner requires to be listed, the bid coordinator enters the carried bidder's name on the subcontractor list of the bid form so it matches the carried price.

error.defect_description: Name on the list differs from the carried bidder.

control.basis: Owner's instructions to bidders: list of major subcontractors with the bid (Nova Scotia guidelines 4.1)

evidence.note: Requirement to list major subcontractors as part of the tender.

steps.name: Recommend the trade award to the owner
steps.description: On construction management work the preconstruction manager writes a recommendation letter with the levelling sheet and sends it to the owner and consultant, who approve the trade before it is let.

error.defect_description: Recommendation omits an exclusion.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; owner approval of trade awards under CM agreements.

steps.name: Wait for the prime bid result or owner approval
steps.description: The package waits for the prime bid opening result, or on CM work for the owner's approval of the recommended trade.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: company low or trade award approved

evidence.note: Weighted: about 15% of stipulated bids are low and most CM trade recommendations are approved; author's estimate.

steps.name: Pass the trade bid to buyout
steps.description: The bid coordinator sends the levelling sheet, quotes, clarifications and scope sheet to supply chain and the project manager so the subcontract can be bought out against the carried price.

error.defect_description: Clarification notes are not passed on with the quote.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; the organisation file links trade bids to scm-subcontract-buyout.

steps.name: Notify trade bidders and file the quotes
steps.description: The bid coordinator emails trade bidders the prime result and files the quotes and levelling sheet, which estimators later mine for unit prices.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; courtesy notice to trades.

exceptions.name: Thin coverage
exceptions.description: Fewer than three trades commit, so more firms are invited; if coverage still fails the estimator carries an own-estimate plug.

exceptions.name: Revised quote on bid day
exceptions.description: A bidder adds back an excluded item or revises its price after a clarification call, and the package is re-levelled.

exceptions.name: Unlisted low bidder
exceptions.description: The low bidder is not prequalified; the analyst approves it provisionally or the next bidder is carried.

exceptions.name: Bid depository package
exceptions.description: Mechanical or electrical prices come through the local bid depository about two working days before closing.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from package scope to result filed or passed to buyout
benchmarks.population: Trade packages on Canadian building tenders

evidence.note: Author's estimate: trade invitations go out in the first week of a three to five week tender period; results follow closing within days.
Vendor source; stated figure.

benchmarks.unit: working days before prime bid closing
benchmarks.population: Federal government projects using bid depositories (policy to 2006)

pain_points.description: Quotes arrive in the final hours, so exclusions are skimmed under time pressure and gaps reach buyout.

evidence.note: Ignored qualifications become change orders.

pain_points.description: Coverage chasing by phone takes coordinator time for every package on every bid.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor trade tendering practice; phone chasing common in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Prequalification records go stale (insurance and WSIB certificates), so low bidders need checks on bid day.

evidence.note: The organisation file notes expired certificates as the usual gap in prequalification.

sources.title: What Is Bid Leveling in Construction?
sources.supports: Bid leveling steps: log bids, build a scope matrix (included, excluded, alternate, unclear), compare line items, send question lists and document conversations, carry unresolved items conservatively, select on more than price; bids often arrive in the final hours or minutes before the deadline; manual leveling takes 2-4 hours per major scope; a $100M hospital may have 25+ scope packages; a bid 15% below the others warrants scrutiny; ignored qualifications become change orders. Undated vendor page.

sources.title: Contracting Policy, Appendix N: Bid Depositories
sources.publisher: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat (archived copy, Library and Archives Canada)
sources.supports: Bid depositories run by local construction associations receive sealed trade bids so prime contractors have firm prices in time to compile their bids; used for trade bids on federal projects over $200,000 when named in the tender; trade bids close normally two working days before prime bids; withdrawals up to six hours before prime closing; with two or fewer trade bids the authority may negotiate. Federal policy of 1992-2006, used here as a description of depository practice.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Public Sector Construction Contract Guidelines (June 2017)
sources.supports: Prequalification of bidders with a published minimum score (often 70-80 of 100); solicitation documents list major subcontractors, bid security, CCDC contract form; bonding recommended at $500,000 and over; subcontracts of $250,000 or more should carry contract security; addenda no later than 5 business days (major) or 3 business days (minor) before closing and closing extended at least 1 business day when needed; late bids rejected; amendments and withdrawals allowed up to closing; withdrawal after opening only for serious demonstrable error within 2 business days; within 48 hours of opening bidders may be asked for safety certifications, other subcontractors and price breakouts; bids over the estimate may be negotiated or re-tendered; letter of award binds the contractor to sign; contract security within 10 days of award; bid security of unsuccessful bidders returned within 30 days; international trade agreements may require 40-day postings.

assumptions: One case is one trade package on one bid; about 25-35 packages run in parallel for each stipulated bid.

The organisation file lists subcontractor and supplier trade bids as triggers; here they are inputs, because a case starts when estimating issues the package, and shares are split across the four internal triggering processes.
Estimator and bid coordinator FTE cover trade work only; the bid's own estimating is in bd-stipulated-bid.
Bid depository use (12% of packages) applies mainly to Western and Atlantic mechanical and electrical trades; the depository rule cited is the federal policy, used to describe practice.
Role costs and titles from the organisation file; prequal-analyst is an organisation file role not listed for this process.

Hands-on time implies about 12 FTE of bid coordinator work on trade packages; with the pipeline and stipulated bid steps that exceeds the organisation file's 10 bid coordinators, so the stated 8 FTE assumes estimators do part of the coverage chasing and quote logging themselves.
No equipment, vehicles or crews are tied up; office roles have no shift pattern.
